newsitem.title: USA: Stocks bounce back after three sessions of losses.
newsitem.headline: Stocks bounce back after three sessions of losses.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks roared into the plus column Thursday, clawing back after three straight sessions of profit-taking losses.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 36.64 points at 7,755.35, nearing its June 13 record closing high of 7,782.04.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 13-9 on active volume of 296 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 8.55 points at 1,440.98.
Analysts said the trading volume had improved ahead of Friday's "triple-witching" expirations of stock index futures, options and options on individual stocks.
"Its just really setting itself up for the options expiration tomorrow," said Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage.
"Whatever reason you had for it to go up in the beginning of the week you still have. Once the expirations are out of the way, we'll go on with what we were going to do," he said.
The market was also buoyed by news that new claims for state unemployment insurance rose to 347,000 in the latest week from 339,000 a week earlier.

Economists said the surprising jump in weekly jobless claims suggested the labour market might be cooling slightly and ought to make the Federal Reserve feel even more comfortable about keeping interest rates on hold at its July meeting.
In another report, the government said the U.S. trade deficit rose 7.8 percent in April to $8.4 billion as record exports were not enough to offset record imports.
The Commerce Department said exports were up 0.2 percent to a record $78.36 billion in April. Imports increased 0.9 percent to $86.72 billion.
"Exports are showing considerable strength, which is particularly good news in the face of a strong dollar," said Lynn Reaser, chief economist at Barnett Bank Inc.
The market drew some brief selling early in the session following news of a stronger-than-expected economic report from the regional Philadelphia Federal Reserve.
The Philadelphia Fed's June business activity index came in at 25.2 vs. economists' expectations for a reading of 7.3.
Bill Meehan of Prudential Securities said the report was significant.
"Given the fact we're on Fed watch, a report like that from a region makes people sit up and take pause," he said.
Tobacco stocks rose on word that a settlement with state attorneys general was imminent, with Philip Morris Cos. up 2-1/4 at 47-7/8 and RJR Nabisco Holdings up 1-1/8 to 35-5/8.
Unisys Corp. was up 3/8 at 7-3/8 after the struggling computer maker announced its chairman and chief executive officer, James Unruh, would resign after seven years at the helm.

Digital Equipment was up 3/8 at 37-3/4 after a group of institutional shareholders who own 30 percent to 40 percent of the company stock met to discuss alternatives for the beleaguered company in light of its poor financial and stock performance.
